To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) chitosan, N-trimethylchitosan derivatives (both 20% and the 60% N-methylated derivative) are effective enhancers of octreotide transport across airway epithelial cell monolayers, and b) the mechanism of enhancement is paracellular, as suggested by the in vitro/in vivo correlations.

the polysaccharides chitosan, TMS20 and TMC30 are promising enhancers to improve the bio-availability of octreotide and that the Calu-3 model is a suitable in vitro model to predict absorption kinetics of peptides and proteins across airway epithelia.
chitosan, N-trimethylchitosan and Calu-3 cells are useful in predicting the in vivo absorption of peptides across mammalian airways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel formulation technology for the administration of peptide drugs to the lung.
the development of safe and effective polysaccharide-based formulations for the treatment of lung diseases.
the development of safe and efficient permeation enhancers for the delivery of peptide drugs to the lung.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chitosan and its derivatives are effective enhancers for the absorption of octreotide across the airway epitheliam both in vitro and vivo.
the permeation enhancing effect of chitosan and its derivatives is linearly correlated in vitro and in vitro and can be predicted by the in vitro model.
TMC60 is the most effective and safe polysaccharide enhancer for the delivery of octreotide across the airway epithelum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the in vitro/in vivo approach is useful for the prediction of the mechanism of action, the safety and efficacy of permeation enhancers.
the use of polysaccharides in drug delivery is a safe approach for the development of peptide drug formulations with improved absorption kinetics.
we have shown that the polysaccharide TMC60 can be used as an enhancer to increase absorption of the peptide drug Octreotide across the bronchial epithelium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
polysaccharide permeation enhancement is not a random phenomenon.
in vivo/in vitro correlations can be successfully applied for predicting absorption kinetics of peptides and proteins.
the in vitro-in vivo correlation approach can provide a powerful tool for the rational design of permeation enhancer formulations.
